models._description: Synchronize a record with Microsoft Calendar (AbstractModel mixin)

behavioral_notes.observation: OAuth2 authorization-code flow against the Microsoft identity platform. MicrosoftCalendarService._microsoft_authentication_url builds the consent URL via microsoft.service._get_authorize_uri for scope 'offline_access openid Calendars.ReadWrite' with access_type=offline against login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/authorize (so Microsoft returns a refresh_token). Microsoft redirects back to the /microsoft_account/authentication public controller (in microsoft_account), which POSTs the code to the v2.0/token endpoint via _get_microsoft_tokens to exchange it for access_token + refresh_token + expires_in; these are stored on res.users (microsoft_calendar_rtoken/token/token_validity, group base.group_system) by _set_microsoft_auth_tokens. _get_microsoft_calendar_token lazily refreshes an expired access token (validity < now+1min) by POSTing the refresh_token to the same token endpoint; on HTTP 400/401 (invalid grant / invalid client) it rolls back, wipes the stored tokens + res.users.settings.microsoft_calendar_sync_token, commits and raises a UserError. None of this token lifecycle is visible from field/model metadata.

Bidirectional sync. _sync_microsoft_calendar pulls remote changes (MicrosoftCalendarService.get_events -> Graph /v1.0/me/calendarView/delta, then per seriesMaster /v1.0/me/events/{id}/instances), then (Microsoft->Odoo) calls calendar.event._sync_microsoft2odoo to create/update/cancel Odoo events and recurrences, and (Odoo->Microsoft) calls _get_microsoft_records_to_sync + _sync_odoo2microsoft on records owned by the user that are unsynced or flagged need_sync_m. Conflict resolution is last-modified-wins: _sync_microsoft2odoo parses each mevent.lastModifiedDateTime and only writes the Odoo record if it is >= the record's stored write_date (with an optional lower_bound_range guard via _check_old_event_update_required so a sub-second drift on an old event does not re-mail attendees). _sync_odoo2microsoft routes each record to _microsoft_insert (POST /v1.0/me/calendar/events), _microsoft_patch (PATCH) or _microsoft_delete (DELETE). Two distinct identifiers are tracked: microsoft_id (per-calendar event id, used as the API path) and ms_universal_event_id (iCalUId, common across calendars, used to match the same event between attendees/recurrences). This cross-system reconciliation is pure runtime behavior absent from metadata.

Odoo->Microsoft writes are deferred to post-commit. The @after_commit decorator registers the Graph API call on cr.postcommit so the outbound HTTP request fires only after the Odoo transaction commits (with a fresh cursor/registry), preventing an event from being created in Microsoft when the Odoo write later rolls back (avoids duplicates after a crash). The no_calendar_sync context key short-circuits sync entirely. On success _microsoft_insert writes back the returned id + iCalUId and clears need_sync_m; a failed patch/delete leaves need_sync_m set so it is retried next cycle. The Graph request timeout is configurable via the microsoft_calendar.graph_timeout system parameter (default 5s). The transactional-boundary coupling and the id/uid write-back are not metadata-derivable.

behavioral_notes.element: incremental delta sync ($deltatoken / nextSyncToken) + 410 fullSyncRequired full-sync fallback; Outlook recurrence-creation guard
behavioral_notes.observation: Polling delta-sync, not a push webhook. MicrosoftCalendarService._get_events_delta sends the stored microsoft_calendar_sync_token as Graph's $deltatoken so only events changed since the last run are returned; the @odata.deltaLink in the final page yields the next $deltatoken, persisted on res.users.settings. When the token is absent (first run) a full sync is performed, windowed to +/- microsoft_calendar.sync.range_days (default 365) around now via startDateTime/endDateTime. If Graph returns HTTP 410 with code fullSyncRequired or SyncStateNotFound, InvalidSyncToken triggers a retry without the token (forced full sync). 'occurrence' items are filtered out of the delta and re-fetched per seriesMaster via /instances to obtain their iCalUId. There is NO Microsoft push/watch channel: syncs are driven by the cron ir_cron_sync_all_cals (res.users._sync_all_microsoft_calendar, every 12h, commits per user) and on-demand by /microsoft_calendar/sync_data. Distinctively, to respect an Outlook anti-spam limitation, calendar.event create/write/unlink raise UserError forbidding recurrence creation/update/deletion from Odoo while sync is active and direct the user to Outlook (_forbid_recurrence_creation / _forbid_recurrence_update). The token-windowing, full-resync fallback and recurrence guard are runtime-only.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration -> Microsoft Graph + identity platform (gap #7, static)
behavioral_notes.observation: Outbound HTTPS integration via python-requests to Microsoft, host allow-listed by assertion in microsoft.service._do_request to login.microsoftonline.com (token endpoint) and graph.microsoft.com (Graph REST: calendarView/delta, events, events/{id}/instances, calendar/events insert/patch/delete/answer). Auth is per-user OAuth2 access_token sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. The admin supplies cal_microsoft_client_id (public, in clear; microsoft_calendar_client_id ICP) and cal_microsoft_client_secret (microsoft_calendar_client_secret ICP, never returned in clear). Videocall links are provisioned through Microsoft Teams (isOnlineMeeting + onlineMeetingProvider='teamsForBusiness'; joinUrl / teams.microsoft.com URLs mapped to videocall_location). No vendored SDK -- the REST client is hand-rolled in utils/microsoft_calendar.py + microsoft_account/models/microsoft_service.py. This external SaaS dependency is invisible to Python model/field metadata and is the defining trait of the module.

classification.rationale: microsoft_calendar is calendar-sync integration infrastructure: it adds no business object of its own (only a sync-state mixin microsoft.calendar.sync, OAuth token fields on res.users, sync-state fields on res.users.settings and a reset wizard) and produces no sellable output. It is a connector that extends the calendar subsystem by wiring Odoo's calendar.event/recurrence to an external SaaS (Microsoft Graph / Outlook Calendar) over OAuth2 + REST. Per Stabell & Fjeldstad this is a support / firm-infrastructure function (activity_class=support). For APQC it maps to 8.0 Manage Information Technology -- specifically the 'manage IT integration / data interoperability' band: the module's whole reason to exist is external-system integration (gap #7, talks to graph.microsoft.com and login.microsoftonline.com), OAuth credential lifecycle management and cross-system data reconciliation, which are IT-management concerns rather than business-capability development. This mirrors its sibling google_calendar and is the deliberate point of departure from its parent calendar.metamodel.json (classified 13.0 Develop and Manage Business Capabilities, i.e. the collaboration/scheduling capability itself): the parent owns the scheduling capability; this child owns the IT plumbing that integrates that capability with a third-party service, which is exactly what 8.0 covers. 13.0 was considered (inherited from the parent/baseline) but rejected because nothing here develops a new business capability -- it operates an external interface; 9.0 'Acquire, Construct, and Manage Assets' was also rejected since no physical/IT asset is managed, only an API connection.

standard_capabilities: OAuth2 connect to a Microsoft 365 account (offline access + refresh token, scope Calendars.ReadWrite)
two-way sync of events and recurrences between Odoo calendar and Outlook calendar
incremental delta sync via calendarView/delta $deltatoken with automatic full-resync on 410 fullSyncRequired
background sync cron (12h) plus on-demand sync from the calendar view
per-user pause / stop / restart and an account-reset wizard (delete in Microsoft/Odoo/both)
Microsoft Teams online-meeting (videocall) link propagation (isOnlineMeeting / teamsForBusiness)
typical_fits: internal users mirroring their Odoo meetings to a personal/work Outlook calendar
self-registered Microsoft Azure app: admin sets client id/secret in Settings
last-modified-wins reconciliation for occasional concurrent edits
common_gaps: no Microsoft push/watch webhook -- latency bounded by the 12h cron unless the view triggers sync
recurrences cannot be created/updated/deleted from Odoo while synced (Outlook anti-spam limitation) -- must be done in Outlook
full-sync window hard-bounded to +/- range_days (default 365); older/farther events excluded
no field-level merge -- whole-event last-modified-wins can drop concurrent edits to other fields
syncs the user's default calendar only; shared/secondary Outlook calendars are not supported
Outlook ErrorOccurrenceCrossingBoundary restricts reordering occurrences within a recurrence
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['res.users']._sync_all_microsoft_calendar()  # run the 12h cron sync for all connected users

How _is_microsoft_insertion_blocked + _get_event_user_m interact to decide which user's token sends an event whose organizer differs from the editor (attendee must not insert on behalf of the owner).
